title: Phase 2: attachments, group chat, cross-tailnet node sharing
description:
What: Implement the Phase 2 feature set as described in kith-architecture.md.

Why: Phase 1 MVP (1:1 text chat, single static binary, minimal web client) is complete and stable. Phase 2 is the next planned milestone: richer message content (attachments), wider conversations (group chat), and extended tailnet reach (cross-tailnet via node sharing).

Features (from kith-architecture.md):

1. Attachments (kith-attach crate — currently empty stub)
   - Blob storage on disk, served over kithd HTTPS, referenced by blobId in JMAP
   - Lazy replication: recipient mailbox fetches from sender on first open
   - maxAttachmentBytes: 104857600 (100 MB per attachment, already in session object)
   - Path traversal and content_type validation at boundary (per CLAUDE.md)
   - API surface: upload (owner), download (owner + authorized peer), blobId references in Message/set

2. Group chat (N-participant fanout)
   - Chat IDs remain deterministic: hex(sha256(sorted_participant_ids joined by \x00))
   - Sender outbox fans out to N recipients; each recipient stores independently
   - No group coordinator node; all fanout is sender-side
   - Peer/deliver payload unchanged; group membership derived from chatId

3. Cross-tailnet via node sharing
   - No code changes required per architecture doc — Tailscale node-sharing makes shared-in nodes appear as peers in WhoIs
   - Work: test and document the node-sharing setup flow; verify peer-identity check accepts shared-in user IDs
   - Write integration test using mocked WhoIs returning a shared-in identity

Non-goals (permanent, per kith-architecture.md):
- No E2EE (Phase 3 only)
- No native desktop client in Phase 2 scope (Tauri deferred)
- No central relay, no federation, no multi-tenant mode

Outcome: kithd supports sending and receiving file attachments, group conversations among N tailnet peers, and verified operation across tailnets via node sharing.
